title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — roles, stop/logprobs, streaming stability & structured output
author: Elena Kim
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility /v1/chat.completions surface to parity with OpenAI's API for roles, stop sequences, logprobs, streaming tokens, function/tool calling and structured response formatting. This PR implements parameter mappings, request validation, streaming stability fixes (SSE + chunking semantics), and structured output normalization so downstream SDKs and customers can migrate with minimal changes.

What this PR does: 
- Add support for 'roles' arrays (system/user/assistant) with canonical validation and legacy fallback.
- Implement 'stop' handling for chat requests (single string or array), integrating with our tokenizer-aware length checks and ensuring proper stream termination.
- Expose 'logprobs' and 'top_logprobs' fields in the non-streamed response; ensure correct mapping from our scoring pipeline to OpenAI's semantics.
- Structured output: normalize assistant responses to include choices[].message vs choices[].text depending on request; support function_call.name and function_call.arguments in streaming and non-streaming paths.
- Streaming stability: fix partial-chunk buffering causing duplicated tokens for long messages; improve SSE framing and backpressure handling so clients receive deterministic termination events.
- Tests: add unit + integration tests for param parsing, streaming end-of-stream behavior, function calling roundtrips, and response formatting; update API contract tests used by SDKs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Parameter mapping and validation implemented
- [x] Streaming fixes implemented and manually tested with example clients
- [x] Structured output normalization implemented and documented
- [x] Unit & integration tests added
- [x] SDK compatibility test updates (python/ts)
- [x] Release notes drafted

Notes on compatibility: The endpoint accepts both legacy completion-style inputs (prompt/text) and chat-structured messages. Where ambiguous, chat messages take precedence. Function calling fields are preserved in the response; existing Redwood SDKs will prefer message-based accessors when present.

Performance considerations: Stop-sequence handling adds minimal overhead (token-level checks are already in our runtime). Streaming buffering change reduces tail-latency variance at the cost of a small increase in memory for in-flight streams; measured in benchmarks as <2% throughput impact on synthetic workloads but ~20% reduction in duplicate-token incidents observed during manual testing.

Related PRs/Files: see files changed. Linked Linear tickets: ENG-1143 (chat parity work), ENG-1178 (streaming stability).

- OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: roles & chat.messages support
- stop parameter support (string | [string]) with tokenizer-aware termination
